newsitem.title: UK: Texaco, Gulf fined 200,000 stg for UK refinery blas.
newsitem.headline: Texaco, Gulf fined 200,000 stg for UK refinery blas.

text.p: Texaco Ltd and Chevron Corp unit Gulf Oil (Great Britain) Ltd were each fined 100,000 stg and ordered to pay costs of 143,700 stg after a huge explosion at their Pembroke oil refinery in July 1994, the Press Association reported on Friday.
The explosion and fire caused extensive damage to the plant in west Wales, injured 26 people and damaged nearby properties.
The judge, Justice Morland, said the fine reflected public concern and condemnation of the offences, but he accepted that no individual employee was to blame for the accident.
The prosecution was brought by the U.K.'s safety watchdog, the Health and Safety Executive.
The Crown court in Swansea heard a catalogue of errors and equipment failure led to a massive explosion which was heard 30 miles away, the Press Association reported.
The prosecution said the operators at the 500 acre site failed to shut down the system despite a warning hours before the explosion that equipment had failed.

A combination of equipment failures and shortcomings by staff had contributed to a dangerous build-up of liquid in a catalytic-cracking unit which converted crude oil into lighter products such as petrol and diesel.
A fierce thunderstorm earlier in the day had already caused problems at the plant when a malfunction of a crucial valve started a chain of events leading to the explosion.
Unknown to staff in the operations control room, a large quantity of flammable liquid was diverted into pipework not designed to take such pressure.
About 20 tonnes of liquid mixed with vapour burst into the atmosphere because part of the pipework was corroded.

At the start of the hearing Martin Heslop QC, for both companies, entered guilty pleas. Each company faces two charges that they failed to ensure the reasonable safety of employees, sub-contractors and members of the public.
Texaco, in partnership with Gulf, were forced to shut the plant down for several weeks during a repair operation reported to have cost 50 million stg.
